Dear Secretary Reese: 
 
Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act1 and Part 35 of the rules and 
regulations2 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission”), the Commission’s 
Order Granting Rescission and Abeyance Requests3 and the Commission’s Order Instituting 
Proceeding Under Section 206 of the Federal Power Act,4 SunZia Transmission, LLC (“SunZia 
Transmission”) hereby tenders for filing amendments to its Transmission Owner Transmission 
Tariff (“TO Tariff”)5 to incorporate changes to those provisions of the TO Tariff necessary to 
track changes being made simultaneously by the California Independent System Operator 
Corporation (“CAISO”) to its Open Access Transmission Tariff (the “CAISO Tariff”) to 
facilitate the fast and reliable interconnection of new large loads and co-located loads to the 
CAISO-managed transmission system.  The revisions to the SunZia Transmission TO Tariff are 
submitted and designated in accordance with Order No. 7146 and the Commission’s e-Tariff 
filing requirements.

I. 
BACKGROUND 
SunZia Transmission is an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of Pattern Energy Group 
LP and has developed, constructed and recently placed into commercial operation, an 
approximately 552-mile, bi-pole, high voltage, direct current (“HVDC”) 500 kV transmission 
line (the “Transmission System”) with a transmission capacity of 3,021 MW in New Mexico and 
Arizona that connects generation resources in the Southwest with markets and customers in 
California and Arizona.7  SunZia Transmission commenced construction of the Transmission 
System in 2023 and placed the Transmission System into commercial operations in April, 2026.  
The Transmission System has been developed as a merchant transmission project with negotiated 
rate authority contingent on the allocation of its transmission capacity pursuant to an open 
solicitation process reviewed and approved by the Commission.8 
 
As a result, the entire capacity of the Transmission System is committed to two 
Subscribers, SunZia Wind South LLC and SunZia Wind North LLC (collectively, the “SunZia 
Wind Companies”), both of which own and operate wind-powered electric generating facilities 
located in Lincoln, Torrance, and San Miguel Counties, New Mexico (the “SunZia Wind 
Projects”).  SunZia Transmission will provide to the SunZia Wind Companies firm point-to-
point transmission service for the entire rated capacity of the Transmission System over a thirty-
year term9 from the Point of Receipt at the Pete Heinrich 345 kV AC Switchyard to the Point of 
Delivery at the Salt River Project Agricultural Improvement and Power District’s (“SRP”) Pinal 
Central 500 kV Substation pursuant to Amended and Restated Transmission Service Agreements 
 
7 
SunZia Transmission and the New Mexico Renewable Energy Transmission Authority (“RETA”) have entered 
into a lease arrangement pursuant to which RETA owns the physical assets of the Transmission System.  
SunZia Transmission and RETA are both responsible for the co-development of the Transmission System, 
while SunZia Transmission is responsible for the construction and financing of the Transmission System and is 
the owner of the capacity rights created by the Transmission System.  RETA is a state authority established by 
the New Mexico legislature in 2007 and charged with implementing the New Mexico Renewable Energy 
Authority Transmission Act, NMSA 1978 § 62-16A-1, et seq. (the “Act”).  As an authority or instrumentality 
of the State of New Mexico, RETA is not a “public utility” within the meaning of Section 201 of the FPA.  See 
16 U.S.C. § 824(f) (2019).  Under the Act, RETA is authorized to plan, finance, develop and acquire 
transmission and storage projects (transmitting or storing at least 30% renewable energy) in order to promote 
the development of renewable energy in New Mexico.  For purposes of this filing, SunZia Transmission is 
considered the Transmission Owner in interest of the Transmission System pursuant to the lease arrangement 
described above. 
8  
Allocation of Capacity on New Merchant Transmission Projects and New Cost-Based, Participant-Funded

9  
The initial thirty-year term commenced on July 30, 2026.  Each of the SunZia Wind Companies has roll-over 
rights to continue service at the end of the initial term.

In addition, the SunZia Wind Companies have acquired 2,131 MW of long-term, firm 
point-to-point transmission service from the Pinal Central 500 kV Substation to the Palo Verde 
500 kV Hub (which interconnects to the CAISO-controlled transmission system) through a 
number of transmission service agreements with SRP (1,500 MW), the Desert Southwest Region 
of the Western Area Power Administration (“WAPA”) (300 MW), and Tucson Electric Power 
Company (“TEP”) (331 MW) with initial terms ranging from five years to twenty years and, in 
each case with the SunZia Wind Companies having roll-over rights thereafter (collectively, the 
“Arizona Entitlements”).11  SunZia Transmission has obtained authorization from the SunZia 
Wind Companies to administer the Arizona Entitlements (subject at all times to each SunZia 
Wind Company’s right to use the Arizona Entitlements for the transmission of electricity to the 
Palo Verde Hub for the benefit of the SunZia Wind Projects) and to grant CAISO operational 
control of the Arizona Entitlements consistent with the Transmission Rights and Curtailment 
Instructions that will be provided by SunZia Transmission consistent with applicable terms and 
conditions of the WAPA, SRP and TEP tariffs and business practices.  
 
On September 22, 2023, in Docket No. ER23-2917-000, the CAISO filed proposed 
revisions to the CAISO Open Access Transmission Tariff (the “CAISO Tariff”) to implement a 
Subscriber Participating Transmission Owner  (“SPTO”)  model to facilitate access by merchant 
and participant-funded projects located outside of California to the CAISO transmission system, 
furthering State and Federal goals of increasing access to out-of-state carbon-free generating 
resources.  The Commission accepted the CAISO’s proposed tariff changes by order issued 
March 12, 2024.12  On January 14, 2024, SunZia Transmission applied to become an SPTO and, 
on May 23, 2024, the CAISO Board of Governors approved the SunZia Transmission 
application.  As a result, when the Transmission System entered commercial operation in April 
9, 2026, operational control of the Transmission System and the Arizona Entitlements was 
granted by SunZia Transmission to CAISO pursuant to the CAISO’s Transmission Control 
Agreement at which time the SunZia Transmission Open Access Transmission Tariff (“OATT”) 
was withdrawn.13  As a result, the CAISO Tariff now governs future transmission and 
interconnection service over the Transmission System (subject to the rights and obligations of

On October 21, 2024, SunZia Transmission filed with the Commission its proposed TO 
Tariff pursuant to which its transmission facilities and contractual entitlements would be placed 
under the operational control of CAISO and made available to provide transmission and 
interconnection service under the CAISO Tariff.  By order issued April 17, 2025, the 
Commission accepted SunZia Transmission’s TO Tariff for filing, to become effective on the 
date on which operational control of the transmission facilities and contractual entitlements of 
SunZia Transmission is granted to CAISO.15  The Commission found that the rates, terms and 
conditions of the proposed TO Tariff had been shown to be just and reasonable with one 
exception – the rate design used to calculate the Non-Subscriber Usage Rates set forth in the TO 
Tariff.  On that issue, the Commission found that the filing raised issues of material fact that 
cannot be resolved based on the record before the Commission.16   
 
 
14  During SunZia Transmission’s transition to SPTO status, SunZia Transmission and CAISO entered into an 
Applicant Participating Transmission Owner Agreement (the “APTOA”) pursuant to which the parties agreed 
that the CAISO Tariff govern requests for interconnection with and transmission service over the Transmission 
System. The APTOA was filed by CAISO with the Commission on July 5, 2024 in Docket No. ER24-2471-
000 and was accepted for filing by the Commission on September 3, 2024, and made effective on September 4, 
2024.  California Independent System Operator Corporation, 188 FERC ¶ 61,151 (2024).  On July 8, 2024, in 
Docket No. ER24-2473-000, SunZia Transmission filed revisions to its OATT to amend Sections 17 and 18 to 
notify current and prospective customers that, upon the effective date of the APTOA, all requests for 
transmission or interconnection service on the Transmission System will be processed by CAISO in 
accordance with the CAISO Tariff.  The SunZia Transmission OATT revisions were accepted for filing by the 
Commission on September 4, 2024, and to align with the APTOA, was made effective as of September 4, 
2024.  SunZia Transmission, LLC, Docket No. ER24-2473-000 (Sept. 4, 2024) (unpublished letter order).

SunZia Transmission is in a unique position with respect to its compliance with the 
Commission’s directives in the Order to Show Cause for several reasons.  First, SunZia 
Transmission does not directly serve load and, accordingly, there are no provisions in its TO 
Tariff that address the interconnection of the load to the SunZia Transmission System.  As a 
result, the SunZia Transmission TO Tariff is silent with respect to load interconnections and 
there is no need to modify the Tariff to address the interconnection of large or co-located loads. 
Second, the SunZia Transmission System is not located within the service territory of a load 
serving participating transmission owner within the CAISO market that is subject to the Order to 
Show Cause and that will be submitting tariff changes in response to the Order to Show Cause.  
The SunZia Transmission System is embedded within the service territories of Arizona and New 
Mexico load-serving entities that are not subject to the Order to Show Cause or any of the other 
Orders to Show Cause issued to regional transmission operators or independent system operators 
throughout the country.  Finally, Section 8 of the SunZia Transmission TO Tariff states that all 
requests for interconnection to the SunZia Transmission System must be directed in the first 
instance to CAISO with notice of such request being provided to SunZia Transmission.  Thus, 
CAISO is responsible for managing the generator interconnection process for the SunZia 
Transmission System with SunZia Transmission supporting that process through the undertaking 
of studies on the impact of the interconnection on the System. Any changes to the generation 
interconnection process to facilitate the interconnection of co-located load to the transmission 
system must be set forth in the CAISO Tariff, in which case SunZia Transmission will propose 
conforming changes to its TO Tariff to remain consistent with the CAISO’s changes. 
 
II. 
DESCRIPTION OF FILING 
Consistent with the description above as to SunZia Transmission’s unique and limited 
role in the interconnection process overall, Section 8 of the TO Tariff has been amended to 
clarify that the CAISO Tariff will continue to control with respect to the interconnection of 
Generating Units, energy storage co-located with Large Load and Co-located Generating Units 
with Large Loads.  In proposing these limited changes to its TO Tariff, SunZia Transmission 
reserves the right, following review of the proposed tariff changes filed by the other Participating 
Transmission Owners (“PTOs”) that are subject to the Commission’s Order to Show Cause, to 
amend this filing to propose additional changes to ensure consistency among all similarly-
situated PTOs.   
Finally, consistent with its comments made during the stakeholder process, SunZia 
Transmission continues to support the need to apply these enhanced Large Load interconnection 
procedures to Electrically Proximate Loads.  CAISO has explained that the need for such 
changes within the CAISO footprint in California will be addressed following the submission of 
the Large Load compliance filing.  SunZia Transmission supports the commencement of that 
effort as soon as possible because the value proposition and the question surrounding how to 
study the interconnection of electrically proximate large load and generation in tandem (similar 
to co-located load and generation) are unique when applied to the SunZia Transmission System 
in New Mexico and Arizona.

The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese 
November 16, 2026

IV. 
PROPOSED EFFECTIVE DATE 
SunZia Transmission proposes an effective date of sixty days after the Commission 
issues an order on this compliance filing for the changes to its TO Tariff.  A period of sixty days 
after the Commission approves this filing will allow enough time for SunZia Transmission to 
seamlessly transition to the new processes.  Because a precise effective date is not known at this 
time, SunZia Transmission is submitting this filing with a 12/31/9998 effective date for the tariff 
records, and, if necessary, will make a compliance filing to apply the actual effective date once 
known.

VI. 
CONCLUSION 
In accordance with the foregoing, SunZia Transmission respectfully requests that the 
Commission accept the proposed revisions to its TO Tariff as just and reasonable and consistent 
with its obligations under the Order to Show Cause and grant an effective date of sixty days after 
the Commission’s order on this filing.
